label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: A cookie consent dialog was open on arrival with no focus placed in it; I had to use the elements list to reach Decline, and focus was lost to the top of the page after dismissing it.
Many product cards have several identical Add to Cart buttons with no product name, so I could not tell which product a button belonged to without counting positions.

After pressing Add to Cart nothing was announced: the button just turned disabled and the cart count still read 0. I only learned the item was added after re-reading twice, when the cart drawer appeared.

The cart drawer opened as plain content with no dialog role and the link Cart marked expanded, while the rest of the page stayed fully reachable behind it; the quantity controls are links named Decrease quantity and Increase quantity rather than buttons.

On the checkout page focus starts at the top with nothing focused, the Pay now button is disabled with no explanation, and the billing address and payment methods sit in one long form with several empty Status regions, which makes the page hard to follow by ear.
